phases.title: Before the doors open
phases.goal: Remove what costs something on every request, cold start, scheduled run or agent session, with small and safe changes, and make the changes that are cheapest while no real store, order or picture exists. No step here waits for the owner's answer or for a later phase. Steps 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 go first; 0.23 comes before 0.24, 0.9 before 0.11, and 0.28 before 0.29. Otherwise no step waits for another.
phases.notice: Almost nothing on a screen changes, apart from two faults a shopper would have met on day one (empty search thumbnails, and a button with no fill on the status and report pages) and admin lists that show 100 rows at a time. Cold pages answer sooner, an admin screen loads about half the script, a store page stops asking the server for a wishlist and stock nobody has, and the database falls from 731 MB to about 230 MB.

steps.title: Put the review's scripts and lists in the repo
steps.what: The detectors this plan's checks name exist only in the review's scratch folder: the refined copy counter, the twin counter, the import-reach walker, the trace summers and four deletion lists. Copy them to docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/ and lists/, beside the seven scripts already there, and point every done-when at the repo path. Do this first: steps 0.6, 0.8 and 0.36 are proved with these scripts, and phase 1 turns them into tests.
steps.done_when: Each script, run with node from a fresh checkout, gives its number again (41 twin pairs, 4,098 exact copied lines across files, 1,308 files reached by /api/visit), and rg 'scratchpad' over this plan and the findings files prints nothing.
steps.platform: The scripts read the whole of src, so the platform's files and routes are counted with the stores'.

steps.title: Store a daily reading of production, so every later step has a 'before'
steps.what: Production's statistics are read by hand and no reading is kept. Add one statement to the daily route (src/app/api/cron/subscription-reminders/route.ts). It writes a dated reading into a small platform table, kept 90 days. The reading holds the 40 costliest and the 40 most-called statements of the app's role (Postgres has already stripped the values), each commerce table's rows, size and scan counters, and the size of each schema. No screen yet: step 1.13 shows the reading and adds the flags, and closes the gap this step starts on. Land it before the fixes, so their 'before' is on record.
steps.done_when: In production the new table holds two days of readings before step 0.23 is deployed, and an int test shows the daily statement writing one row for each commerce table and at most 80 statement rows.
steps.platform: The reading is the platform's own table, and it counts Kaizena Flow's store and its null-store rows with every other.

steps.title: Let the deploy job, not a visitor, meet the first cold page
steps.what: scripts/await-deploy.mjs waits for /api/health and stops. Add page checks from SMOKE_PAGES (Kaizena Flow's home and one page of the template store), so the job pays the first draw and a page that answers 500 fails the run. prerenderedShops() also returns the house store's markets while the switch is on, so kaizenaflow.com is built with each deploy, and CI seeds a house store with the switch on. The review measured Kaizena Flow's front page in a form production no longer serves: measure production's again and write it into docs/performance.md. Land this before steps 0.4 to 0.8: each of them changes what loads cold, and this is the check that catches a missed import in production.
steps.done_when: src/lib/await-deploy.test.ts shows that a page answering 500 fails the job, and after a deploy the release job's log lists Kaizena Flow's home and one template-store page with status 200, their bytes, and the cache header of a prerendered page.
steps.platform: Kaizena Flow's own front page is the first page checked, and it is prerendered with every deploy.

steps.title: Cut the two import hubs: the unused schema and the chat module's helpers
steps.what: src/db/client.ts hands the 19,614-line Drizzle schema to a query builder nobody calls, so 481 table definitions are built at every cold start: make the import type-only and call drizzle({ client: pool }), three lines. The four /api/visit beacons, /api/recommendations/events and /api/docs/feedback take sameSite and two more small helpers through src/server/chat-route.ts, which brings the chat, the AI layer and the support desk with it: import them from the files that define them. In the same change correct the note on the Postgres driver in the code review's dependency item.
steps.done_when: After pnpm build, rg -l --no-ignore -F orders_store_placed_idx .next/server -g '*.js' | wc -l prints 0 (6 today), pnpm db:check exits 0, and a next analyze export shows /api/visit at or under 710 modules (1,890 today).
steps.platform: The same client and beacons serve the platform admin and Kaizena Flow's site, so their cold starts lose the same 115 to 135 ms.

steps.title: Load sharp, the font parser and the AI manager's engine when they are used
steps.what: Thirteen server modules import sharp or opentype.js at the top, so the image library loads with the proxy and about 740 routes that draw no picture: one helper, src/server/sharp-load.ts, returns the module on first use, as browser.ts does for Chromium. Two admin action files load the AI manager's whole server side with every admin page: load src/server/owner-tools.ts when the assistant is first used. Build the tool catalogue's JSON Schema when tools are first listed, not at import (MCP_TOOLS goes).
steps.done_when: src/server/lazy-packages.scan.test.ts passes with 0 static value imports of sharp or opentype.js outside tests and sharp-load.ts (13 today), a next analyze export shows /admin/[store]/orders without src/server/owner-tools.ts at or under 2,050 modules (2,349 today), and rg -n 'MCP_TOOLS' src prints nothing.
steps.platform: The platform admin's pages drop the same engine, and its assistant loads it on first use like a store's.

steps.title: Cut the import cycle of 229 server files
steps.what: 229 files of src/server import each other in one cycle, so almost every route loads everything; six lazy imports and four moved helpers open it. Start where shoppers' pages enter: customers.ts loads privacy-erasure inside deleteCustomer, the bought SQL fragment and storeObligations() move to small files of their own, and orders.ts loads providerOf at its one use. Then the rest, one file's edges per commit: four pure helpers move to src/lib and the async calls become lazy imports. In the same pass take two more edges off every store page: the three-line key reader that brings Stripe (encryptionKey leaves settings.ts) and the theme store section that brings sharp. A lazy import changes the order modules load in (D440), and four of the cuts are on order and payment paths. So land it after step 0.3, and after each deploy open a store page, an admin page and /sitemap.xml in production and delete a test shopper's account.
steps.done_when: The import walker of step 0.1 prints a largest cycle of 19 files or fewer in src/server (229 today) and 760 files or fewer behind src/app/s/[store]/[market]/page.tsx (1,419 today), and a next analyze export shows /s/[store]/[market] at or under 1,800 modules and 8.2 MB with no stripe module and no src/server/theme-store.ts (2,419 modules and 11,944 KB today).
steps.platform: The cycle is one graph: the platform's pages and routes leave it in the same commits.

steps.title: Give code outside the admin its own small word modules, so the admin's words leave shoppers' routes
steps.what: src/lib/admin-text.ts imports all 136 catalogue files in both languages, and 35 files outside the admin import it. So 802 of 830 server entries, the proxy and every storefront page load 2.8 MB of words. Add one module per area that outside code reads (18 areas, src/lib/admin-words/{stem}.ts) and move the 35 importers to them. A scan test keeps the registry out of everything but src/app/admin and src/components/admin.
steps.done_when: src/lib/admin-text-reach.scan.test.ts passes with no value import of lib/admin-text outside src/app/admin and src/components/admin (35 files today) and at most 37 catalogue files in the closure of src/proxy.ts, /api/visit and the storefront layout (135 today).
steps.platform: Kaizena Flow's public site and sign-in pages read their areas through the same small modules, and the platform's areas are among the 18.

steps.title: Make a language translated by AI cost what it uses: at start, per document and per minute
steps.what: The start hook (src/instrumentation.ts) loads 856 modules, among them the translating tools, ai.ts and auth.ts, then reads every AI-translated language whole before the first request, and each instance polls the table every minute. Split the interface-text reader from the translating tools. Read at start with two statements, whatever the number of languages, and build a language on first read. Poll a one-row version stamp every ten minutes, only where such a language is served. uiTextsFor() sends the browser its 114 texts, not all 1,673: 93 KB to under 9 KB in every document of such a store. The search-cache prune that the same finding names leaves the five-minute list in step 0.31.
steps.done_when: In src/server/languages.int.test.ts uiTextsFor(lang) holds exactly the 114 browser keys in under 9,000 bytes for a fully translated language (92,809 today), a unit test shows startUi() issuing 2 statements, and the import walker of step 0.1 counts 60 source files or fewer behind src/instrumentation.ts (383 today) with no src/server/ai.ts.
steps.platform: Kaizena Flow's own site in more than one language (D312) reads through the same reader, so it gains the same start and the same document.

steps.title: Take Supabase's client, zod and the builder's English off every signed-in screen
steps.what: Three stray imports put 481 KB on 432 of 449 admin routes: typingIn() and AdminServiceWorker sit in files that pull in zod and the builder's English catalogue, and session.tsx imports the whole Supabase client for a listener. Move the two helpers to files of their own, take the English default of responsive-edit.tsx out of the keyboard sheet, and load the Supabase client with import() once the page is idle. Drop the 'setup' words area that every admin document carries and nothing reads. Kaizena Flow's public front page loads the same three through its sign-in link: check it in the same change.
steps.done_when: After pnpm build, .next/diagnostics/route-bundle-stats.json shows /admin/[store] at or under 700,000 bytes (1,194,862 today), no route's first-load chunks hold 'GoTrueClient' (432 routes today), 'Set for {size}' is only on the builder's routes (423 today), and 'ZodError' is in at most 160 routes (432 today).
steps.platform: The frame is shared: every /admin/platform screen drops the same 481 KB.

steps.title: Keep the page builder and the rich text editor off screens that do not edit a page
steps.what: Lists, previews and editors share one views file, so 13 previews and the page lists load the 3.3 MB builder. Orders, customers, deals and the product editor load the rich text editor for custom fields the store may not have: 34 screens outside the builder. Split the views file, and load the custom-field editor with next/dynamic where a screen draws it.
steps.done_when: After pnpm build, .next/diagnostics/route-bundle-stats.json shows no route outside the builder's family with 'ProseMirror' in its first-load chunks (34 today, and 13 previews), /admin/[store]/pages/[pageId]/preview at or under 1,450,000 bytes (3,303,372 today) and /admin/[store]/orders/[orderId] at or under 1,350,000 (1,998,644 today).
steps.platform: The platform's page lists and previews are the same files, and its screens with custom fields load the editor the same way.

steps.title: Take two whole tables out of client scripts: the Work invoice's words and the AI manager's tool definitions
steps.what: The Work invoice screen imports the whole admin catalogue in both languages: one 1.7 MB chunk, on the largest route in the admin (4.27 MB). Hand it its words as props. The AI manager's chat loads every tool definition, the admin map and the Norwegian page list (437 KB) to show a label and a page name: keep tool labels and page names only. Do the chat right after step 0.9: once zod is off the frame, this chunk would otherwise fetch it on first opening.
steps.done_when: After pnpm build, route-bundle-stats.json shows no first-load chunk over 600,000 bytes (one of 1,704,595 today) and at most 26 routes over 1,300,000 bytes (90 today), and e2e/signed-in/ai-manager-panel.spec.ts counts at most 130,000 bytes of script on first opening the AI manager (496,206 today).
steps.platform: Work's account-level invoice screen is the one named, and the platform's AI manager opens the same chat.

steps.title: Stop prefetching what a press cannot use on stores and on Kaizena Flow's site
steps.what: Set prefetch off on the language, currency and country links (src/components/view-menu.tsx: a press never opens the page they fetch), on links that leave their root layout, on the footer's legal links and on the six links from Kaizena Flow's pages to /admin and to stores. Today a phone home page read to the footer makes 47 router requests, 24 of them for other views, and Kaizena Flow's front page fetches two /admin answers, six admin scripts and the admin's stylesheet.
steps.done_when: e2e/prefetch.spec.ts (new) passes with 0 router prefetch requests for another view on the phone home read to the footer (24 today) and at most 23 in all (47), 0 on the /s/demo front door (12 today), and 0 requests to /admin after loading / (2 and one stylesheet today).
steps.platform: Kaizena Flow's own front page is the page that stops fetching /admin.

steps.title: Fetch the admin's rail and list rows when a link is pointed at
steps.what: An admin screen makes 23 to 46 router requests at rest, and about 25 again after every save, to fetch nearly the same loading skeleton twelve times. Add AdminLink (src/components/admin/ui/link.tsx) on a small PolicyLink with the policy 'intent', and use it in the rail, the store menu, the account menus and the rows of every list: a link is fetched when the pointer or focus reaches it. View store is never fetched, since the press leaves the admin. A touch or keyboard press then shows the pending bar for one round trip before the skeleton. Step 2.6 later widens PolicyLink to the storefront.
steps.done_when: e2e/signed-in/prefetch.spec.ts (new) counts 0 router prefetch requests in the 3 s after the admin home loads (28 today), at most 2 after hovering one rail link, and 0 for product editors after the Products list loads (8 on a four-row list today).
steps.platform: The platform admin's rail and lists are the same components.

steps.title: End the prefetch loop on /s/ addresses, and write both router settings down
steps.what: On the local build and in CI, listing and search pages at /s/{store} addresses ask for one link's @drawer/[...rest] segment about 165 times a second without end. Set optimisticRouting: false in next.config.ts, with the reason and when it may go, and hold it with a spec that counts requests after load. Write partialPrefetching: false beside it as a recorded choice: unset, Next warns on every build and start, and the next major release will choose for the app. Step 2.8 decides whether to adopt it.
steps.done_when: e2e/prefetch.spec.ts 'a store page goes quiet' passes in CI's e2e job on its three pages (fewer than 60 router prefetch requests in the 3 s after load and none in the next 2 s; the search page makes 624 in 4 s today), and pnpm build prints no partialPrefetching warning.
steps.platform: The platform has no listing at an /s/ address of its own; load the theme store's list in the same spec.

steps.title: Make no server call after load for a visitor with nothing to fetch
steps.what: Every store page asks /wishlist/saved, a function call and a proxy run for a 15-byte answer: ask only when a marker cookie says the visitor has saved something, and list the cookie in KNOWN_COOKIES. Every page with a product grid loads the tile island and asks /api/shop/tiles for stock with three statements, though both tile switches are off by default: draw no island and make no call while they are off. The search results page posts for suggestions nobody typed for: ask after a key or a focus.
steps.done_when: docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/measure-routes.mjs lists 0 requests of the page's own after load on all 12 store pages for a new visitor with the tile switches off (one or two on each today: /wishlist/saved on all 12, /api/shop/tiles on two, a POST on the search page), each held by an assertion in e2e/wishlist.spec.ts, e2e/shop-components.spec.ts and e2e/search.spec.ts.
steps.platform: Store-only by the house rule's exception: Kaizena Flow sells plans, not goods, so its site has no wishlist, tile stock or product search to call for.

steps.title: Send shoppers' first scripts only what the page draws
steps.what: Every store route's first scripts carry the admin's common words, the features table, the purposes of 38 cookies in four languages, an unused library, and small parts a plain page never draws (the theme preview stage, the platform's language switch). Split the cookie patterns from their texts (src/lib/cookie-patterns.ts), keep the admin's words and the features table on the server, and load the filter dialog only where a listing draws it. On the product page move cartView() to a server file, so the cart's forms leave its scripts, and load a picker only for the product's own kind.
steps.done_when: The script tags of the server's HTML, nomodule left out, total at most 615,000 bytes raw for /s/demo/no (680,264 today) and at most 690,000 for /s/demo/no/p/demo-keramikkopp (777,785), the product page's own entry chunks total at most 297,000 bytes (315,368), and none of them holds 'Sell to businesses', 'Waiting for payment' or 'Kommer ihåg om du valde ljusa'.
steps.platform: Kaizena Flow's site pages share these first scripts and lose the same 48 to 65 KB.

steps.title: Cut what a menu and a progress poll cost in the admin
steps.what: The store menu is rebuilt with 220 permission lookups on every shell render, 125 ms of blocking CPU: memoise the answers in src/lib/store-nav.ts and src/lib/permissions.ts, keyed on the path and the access only. Progress polls (refresh-while.tsx, pack-pictures.tsx) stop in hidden tabs and ask their job, not for a whole redraw. The notice badge's count runs two statements, not four. How often an untouched tab asks is the owner's choice, in step 2.34.
steps.done_when: The count test in src/lib/store-nav.test.ts shows 110 lookups per menu build (220 today) in under 2 ms (125 ms), rg -n 'setInterval' src/components/admin/refresh-while.tsx src/components/admin/pack-pictures.tsx shows each tick guarded by visibilityState, and a case in src/server/assistant-notices.int.test.ts counts 2 statements for the badge's count (4 today).
steps.platform: The platform admin uses the same shell, menu builder and notice feed.

steps.title: Draw the route once per save
steps.what: At least 39 saves in the admin draw the whole route twice: the action refreshes it, then the browser calls router.refresh() and asks again. Remove the second, file by file with the screen's spec and not by a codemod: a few screens may lean on the second fetch without meaning to. The four editors that push and refresh keep the push. Write the rule beside storeAction's in docs/rules/admin/platform.md: the action refreshes; a client part does not.
steps.done_when: src/components/admin/router-refresh.scan.test.ts holds client router.refresh() calls in the admin at about 50 (90 today) with 0 after an action that always refreshes (36 today), and the signed-in e2e job passes.
steps.platform: The platform admin's saves run through platformAction() and lose the same second draw.

steps.title: Read the products, customers and stores lists a page at a time
steps.what: The Products list sends every product of the store to the browser (about 0.9 KB a product, no limit in listAdminProducts()), and it reads the whole editor context and a per-product check it does not show: 16 or more statements. The customers list groups every order before it cuts to 100, and the platform's Stores list loads everything. Give each a page of 100 with a count and a next page (code review steps 1.13 and 2.10), and let the products list read only what it shows.
steps.done_when: With a store seeded with 500 products the Products document is under 300,000 characters and says '100 of 500', rg -c getEditorContext 'src/app/admin/(gated)/[store]/products/page.tsx' prints nothing, and an integration test shows listCustomers() for a store with 150 customers returning 100 rows and the count.
steps.platform: The platform's Stores list is one of the three lists and pages the same way.

steps.title: Stop asking for what does not change: a store's slug, the theme cards, the hosts list
steps.what: select slug from commerce.stores where id is written by hand in 27 places and is production's most-called statement (560,090 calls in 78 days): use one cached helper, refreshed when a sandbox is kept. A theme's neighbours read the cached card list, not every theme's snapshot again. The list of store domains is parsed once per instance, not two or three times for every link a page draws.
steps.done_when: rg -c 'select slug from commerce[.]stores where id' src --glob '!*.test.ts' sums to at most 3 (27 today), rg -n 'loadCards\(\)' src/server/theme-store.ts shows two call sites (three today), and the new case in src/lib/store-hosts.test.ts shows 1,000 calls of marketPath() with a 1,000-store hosts list calling JSON.parse once (2,000 or more today).
steps.platform: The slug helper and the hosts list are shared code: the platform admin's links and Kaizena Flow's own store read through them.

steps.title: Read the AI connection only to call a model, and give search a ceiling
steps.what: Screens and polls that only draw a button fetch the whole AI connection, key and month's cost included: 12.4 reads for each AI call made. Give them aiAbilities() from a 60-second memo with no key. Sum the month's AI cost from daily rows plus today (37 to 57 ms a call now). A job reads the connection once per run. Search takes the model's name from the memo, so a search answered from the cache reads no connection. A new search_ai budget, per visitor a minute and per store an hour with a monthly token cap as recommendations have, is taken only on a cache miss: past it the search runs by keyword and is never refused. A store's AI settings refresh that store's tag, not AI_TAG for every store (319 cached entries carry it today).
steps.done_when: After a build grep -rl 'ai-providers' .next/server/app --include='*.meta' | wc -l prints 0 (319 today), an int test sends 200 different searches from one visitor in a minute and counts at most the budget's model calls with 0 reads of commerce.ai_providers for a repeated search, limits-enforce.int.test.ts passes with a month of seeded usage split across measured days and today, and in production the reading of step 0.2 shows at most 2 reads of commerce.ai_providers for each row written to ai_usage over a week (12.4 today).
steps.platform: The provider read keeps its platform branch, and the platform's own AI settings refresh the platform's tag only.

steps.title: Work the cart and a shopper's facts out once per request, with no read for a feature that is off
steps.what: The cart page calls cartSummary() twice per view, and each call sends 5 statements to learn that bonus, referrals and checkout rules are not in use. getCustomer(), getCartCount() and stock are read two to four times in one render. Run them through perRequest() (src/server/request-memo.ts), and skip the bonus, referral and rule reads while the store's features do not include them.
steps.done_when: cart-contents.test.ts asserts cartSummary is called once per cart render and ./bonus is not called for a store with features ['shop'], and a unit test of getCartCount() and getCustomer() shows one read each for two calls inside one render (two to four today).
steps.platform: Store-only by the house rule's exception: Kaizena Flow sells plans through Stripe and draws no cart.

steps.title: Filter a store's rows the way its index can serve
steps.what: Postgres cannot answer store_id is not distinct from $1 from an index, so the hottest reads scan every store's rows: about 1.2 billion rows in 78 days on pages, cookie_scans and terms (122 uses in 40 files). One owned() helper writes store_id = $1 for a store and store_id is null for the platform, and the ratchet counts the old wording per file. The cookie scan's every-minute due check gets two indexes on the expression it filters by, and a failing site backs off. Do it before the new page reads of steps 0.24 and 2.16 are written, so they are born right.
steps.done_when: The ratchet's count of 'store_id is not distinct from' in src/server is at most 3 commented column-to-column lines (122 today), a plan test on a seeded table of 200 owners shows an index scan for one owner's pages, and in production seq_tup_read on commerce.cookie_scans grows by under 1 M a day (about 21 M today).
steps.platform: The is-null branch of owned() is the platform's: its pages, terms and cookie scans are found by index too.

steps.title: Read one page, not all of them
steps.what: listPublishedPages() (src/server/pages.ts) selects every published page of a store with its whole content. It has 35 callers; 13 keep one page by id and most of the rest want slugs or titles. It is 781 s of the app's listed statement time: 29 documents a call, 79,778 calls in 78 days. Add publishedPageById(owner, id), cached per page, and a page index (id, slug, titles, dates, flags), and move the find-by-id callers, the legal links, the platform's frame, robots, the sitemaps and llms.txt to them.
steps.done_when: rg -c 'listPublishedPages(' over src without tests gives at most 14 lines (37 today) with no caller that picks one page by id after it, and after a build no prerendered entry of the demo store keeps the page list (45 of 261 today).
steps.platform: Kaizena Flow's own pages are read through the same two functions with a null owner, and src/server/platform-navigation.ts is one of the callers moved.

steps.title: Prune the scheduler's own log
steps.what: pg_cron's run log is 564 MB of the 731 MB database and nothing prunes it. A daily pg_cron job deletes rows older than seven days, and the backlog is emptied once. Cheapest now: after opening the log grows with every schedule.
steps.done_when: In production select min(end_time) from cron.job_run_details is never older than 8 days, and the size by schema in the reading of step 0.2 shows the cron schema under 60 MB after the one-off emptying (564 MB today).
steps.platform: One scheduler: the prune covers the platform's jobs too.

steps.title: Drop the 13 duplicate indexes, and add the test that stops the next one
steps.what: Thirteen indexes duplicate another: orders carries 34, five of them starting with store_id, placed_at. Each costs every order, order line and counted visit one more entry to write. Drop them, concurrently on the hot tables as D569 says, and add src/db/index-duplicates.test.ts, which compares the two places indexes are declared: the schema, and the 46 hand-written ones that pnpm db:check cannot see. Cheapest while the tables are small.
steps.done_when: src/db/index-duplicates.test.ts returns 0 rows (11 today) with 32 indexes on orders (34 today), and pnpm db:check exits 0.
steps.platform: One database: the platform's tables are in the duplicate test.

steps.title: Let the knowledge job read no document when nothing was published
steps.what: The knowledge job reads about 40 whole pages a call every five minutes and re-cuts wordless pages for ever: 91,200 empty transactions in 78 days. A small table, commerce.knowledge_sources, records what was cut for each page, also when the cut is empty. Changed pages are then chosen in SQL before any document is fetched, and a site with nothing cut asks for no AI connection. The hourly full pass stays as a net.
steps.done_when: A new case in src/server/chat.int.test.ts runs syncPageKnowledge twice over a store with a wordless published page and counts zero transactions and zero rows read from published on the second run, and in production a day after the deploy the calls of 'delete from commerce.knowledge_chunks where page_id = $1' rise by no more than the pages published that day (about 1,170 a day today).
steps.platform: Kaizena Flow's own site has chat on null-store rows: the same job serves it and goes idle the same way.

steps.title: Make picture, alt-text and product upkeep cost one statement when nothing changed
steps.what: Three more AI upkeep jobs walk every store every five minutes to find nothing. The picture job re-checks where each picture is used every day by text-searching every page (13,414 date-only updates on 468 rows): use one change stamp per site, and list only owners with a stale item. The alt-text job lists a site only while a picture is due, and gives up on a picture after five tries. The product index embeds on save from every saver, and its platform-wide scan runs hourly behind a minute guard until step 3.3 gives jobs a cadence. Ship the three apart, smallest first.
steps.done_when: sitesDueForAltText() in src/server/alt-texts.int.test.ts returns no row for a finished site, a new src/server/knowledge.int.test.ts shows an idle run of the four upkeep jobs sending the same number of statements for 1 site and for 20, and in production a day after the deploy n_tup_upd on commerce.media_embeddings rises by fewer than 100 with no content change.
steps.platform: Kaizena Flow's own pictures are null-store rows: the same jobs serve them and go idle the same way.

steps.title: Let the listings' check record a try and read only reworded products
steps.what: The listings' check hashes every product on the platform each run, and asks the model again every five minutes for a listing it could not answer: up to 2,880 AI calls a day on answers it cannot read. Record a try (tries and tried_at on commerce.content_screened), stop the run at the first provider error, and choose only new or reworded products by the text marker that step 0.28 adds. A listing recorded as tried is checked a day later. Say in docs/dsa.md what the cap means at opening.
steps.done_when: The two new cases in src/server/content-moderation.int.test.ts pass, and in production select count(*) from commerce.ai_usage where feature = 'content_moderation' and created_at > now() - interval '1 day' is at most the products created or reworded that day plus the notices plus 10.
steps.platform: The listings' check is the platform's own duty under the DSA: one job reads every store's listings.

steps.what: The invoice job re-asks the same waiting stores every five minutes for 120 days: about 127 calls a day with no invoice issued. steps.title: Record every check's seconds and the build's peak memory, with ceilings
steps.what: Not one number of the checks is held, while the production build peaks at about 7.2 GB of 8. scripts/timed.mjs wraps lint, the type check, the unit run, each integration shard, each Playwright run and each build, with ceilings in scripts/ci-budgets.json (25% above the median of the last ten runs; the slowest job a release waits for at 8 minutes). A check fails when a CI step runs outside the recorder. scripts/next-build.mjs prints seconds and peak memory after every build, Vercel's included; scripts/await-deploy.mjs writes the seconds from push to live, and Playwright's JSON reporter gives the tests that passed only on a retry. Turn source maps off in the Vercel build's page worker if a capped build shows it pays (about 4.7 MB of heap per MB of server code), and write both peaks into docs/build-memory.md. pnpm check runs the pre-push rule through the recorder. It holds the build's measures 4, 6 and 7.
steps.done_when: Every CI run's summary lists seconds for lint, the type check, the unit run, each shard, each browser job and the build, the build's peak memory, the seconds from push to live and the retried tests; a run fails above a ceiling in scripts/ci-budgets.json; and docs/build-memory.md has a row for each source-map setting.
steps.platform: One CI and one build serve stores and platform.

steps.title: Give the production build room, and fail a run before it runs out
steps.what: The build has 0.8 GB of room on Vercel's 8 GB machine and was killed once on 11 November, and nothing in this plan is measured to give it a quarter of the machine. Either pay for the 16 GB build machine, with the build cache and the workers back on, or run vercel build in CI and vercel deploy --prebuilt, which makes the deployed build the checked one. Either way scripts/next-build.mjs prints the peak, and a run goes red with the number when the peak passes 75% of the machine. It holds the build's measure 5.
steps.done_when: Ten production builds in a row peak at 75% of their machine or less in the recorder of step 1.20, a trial build above the line turns its run red, and code review step 1.8 is Done.
steps.platform: One build makes the platform admin and Kaizena Flow's site with the stores.
steps.owner_question: Pay for Vercel's 16 GB build machine, or build in CI and deploy the prebuilt output? Without one of the two the build area stops at a B.

steps.title: Watch the scheduler from outside, and run the daily job once
steps.what: The daily job is scheduled twice at the same minute, by pg_cron and by Vercel's cron, so 40 functions can run twice at once. And the scheduler is watched only from inside itself: if pg_cron stops, nothing runs and nothing says so. Point Vercel's one cron (vercel.json) at a small new route that reads the ledger rows of the dispatcher, and of the tick once step 3.1 makes it, and emails the admins when one is over 15 minutes old. pg_cron's own SQL jobs, the log prune of step 0.25 among them, get a ledger row: a job of the daily list reads cron.job_run_details and fails when one's last run failed or the oldest row is over 8 days old. It holds the scheduled area's measure 6.
steps.done_when: vercel.json schedules only the watcher, commerce.cron_jobs.runs for route.subscription-reminders rises by exactly 1 a day, and stopping pg_cron on a test database sends the email within the hour.
steps.platform: One scheduler runs the platform's jobs with the stores', and the email goes to the platform's admins.

steps.title: Count what is in the stylesheet, and read the style text owners write
steps.what: Nothing counts whose classes the sheet holds, or the style text owners add to every document, so two open decisions have no trigger. docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/scripts/stylesheet-audiences.mjs reads the built sheet and prints the bytes each audience alone names: the admin's share is 51.8 KB raw today. steps.title: Measure what a session really loads, and hold source file size
steps.what: Every figure for the written rules is a file size or an estimate at four characters a token. scripts/session-load.mjs reads session transcripts and prints what a session loaded and read: the always-loaded files, each rule or doc read with its bytes, and every '[Omitted long matching line]'. Sample 20 working sessions from before phase 0 and 20 after. If the sample shows whole rule files being read, the plan gets a step that splits the seven rule files by section. Two counts join the code ratchet and only fall: source files over 100 KB (15) and over 2,000 lines (11). It holds the rules area's measure 8.
steps.done_when: node scripts/session-load.mjs over 20 sessions prints the median bytes of rules and docs read per code change, before and after phase 0, into docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11, and src/server/ratchet.baseline.json holds the two file-size counts.
steps.platform: Sessions that work on the platform are in the sample with the rest.

phases.title: Load on demand
phases.goal: The structural half: each page, function, document and AI call loads what it uses, when it uses it. Before opening is the cheapest time for it, and phase 1's budgets show each step as a number that falls. Order where it matters: 2.2 before 2.3, 2.4 before 2.5, 2.14 before 2.15, 2.16 before 2.17 and 2.18, 2.20 before 2.35, 2.36 before 2.37, and 2.27 and 2.29 before 2.30. Step 2.1 is first because it only waits for the owner's yes.
phases.notice: A store page arrives as a static file with nothing in it twice. A product view asks the database for stock and nothing else. A publish redraws one page, not the whole store. Admin screens hand the browser only the words they show, and the builder paints before its editors load. The AI manager answers on a third of the tokens. With the owner's yes, an agent session starts with a quarter of today's standing rules.

steps.title: Leave a map in CLAUDE.md, and bring the always-loaded core under 10.5 KB
steps.what: Every session and subagent loads CLAUDE.md's 295-line feature index (43,361 bytes in all), of which a change needs two to four lines. Replace it with a map of the seven rule files and a three-line look-up, and change src/lib/rules-index.test.ts so it no longer asks for a line per rule: that takes the file under 15 KB. Then move the database, e2e, typed-row and AI-eval how-to into .claude/rules files loaded by path, where a fresh session and a subagent are shown to receive them; otherwise they sit in docs/rules as rules read on demand. Every sentence that guards an action taken without opening a file stays in the core. The docs budget of step 1.1 then holds 10,500 bytes and 160 lines as a hard ceiling. This is the owner's instruction file, so it waits for a yes. It is the largest saving per agent session in the plan: do it the day the answer is in.
steps.done_when: wc -c -l CLAUDE.md prints under 10,500 bytes and 160 lines (43,361 and 448 today; under 15,000 and 200 if only the first yes is given) with every never-sentence still in it, src/lib/rules-index.test.ts passes, and a fresh session that opens src/db/client.ts can quote the database rule's first sentence.
steps.platform: The rules cover stores and platform alike, and the map names the file that holds the platform's rules.
steps.owner_question: CLAUDE.md is your instruction file. First: may its 295-line feature index go, leaving a map of the seven rule files and a three-line look-up (44 KB to under 15 KB per session)? Second, and it can be declined on its own: may the database, e2e, typed-row and AI-eval how-to load only when those folders are opened (to under 10.5 KB)? Without the first yes the rules area cannot reach a B; without the second it stops short of an A, at the 15 KB ceiling.

On a screen 768 px or wider the cart link then opens the cart page directly: no drawer rendered and thrown away, and no prefetch of it. This restructures the storefront's routes: the cart specs and the phone's drawer are the things to watch.

steps.what: Every prerendered store page is 'resuming': a render function runs on each view to place two cart badges and a country hint. steps.what: A press on a built page's product tile, button or picture is a plain anchor: a whole document and 42 requests, where a link inside the app costs 5. steps.what: A real listing prefetches every product tile and up to six swatch links under each: about 96 requests for 48 products, and the test stores are too small to show it. Seed a 48-product category and bound it at 20 router requests read to the end, with swatches on intent. Run the partial-prefetching trial on the product page, the seeded listing, the store home and the admin's orders page, and write its table into docs/performance.md and the decision into docs/decisions.md: either all links to one route share one shell, or the first screen of tiles is fetched on sight and the rest on touch. The next major Next release forces the choice.

steps.what: Listing, search, cart, checkout, account, order, wishlist and cookies pages share one bundle of every working part, 98 KB larger than a built page's. Move the shell of StorePartSection to a server file with no section imports (src/components/store-part-frame.tsx), and give each route a small module that imports its own sections.

steps.what: A store page with a recommending grid downloads 650 KB more once recommendations answer: zod, the page model and all four storefront languages. The grid takes its words as a prop, from the browser files of src/lib/messages, and the scan that keeps the page model out of a store page's first scripts covers its later ones too.

steps.what: One 183 KB sheet serves stores, the site, the docs and the admin: 28% of it styles only the admin, and 3,480 of the 5,931 files Tailwind reads can rename it though no public page draws them. steps.title: Ask the database for stock only on a product view
steps.what: An anonymous view of a prerendered product sends about 18 statements. One answer, stock, changes per view, and it is read twice. Put what only an owner sets (checkout's look, payment state, checkout fields, quote mode, back in stock, price breaks, producer schemes) in one cached read per store and market, src/server/buy-facts.ts, tagged so its writers refresh it, and carry it in the prerendered page. The buy button then no longer waits for payment facts.
steps.done_when: One anonymous GET of a prerendered goods product on a warm production build commits 3 statements or fewer beyond the proxy's (about 16 today) and reads only the inventory tables, by scripts/server-budget.mjs with its budget at 4, and the product page's reads are off the exceptions list of step 1.12.

steps.title: Let a publish make only its own page stale
steps.what: One tag, pages:{store}, covers all of a store's pages, and 55 places refresh it: one publish makes all 261 built pages of the demo render again. Add page:{id} for reads of one page's document, so a change to a page's body makes that page's entries stale. A change other pages show (a title, an address, a header, a footer) stays store-wide. Cache a product layout once per store, not once per product. The alt-text job refreshes a store's tags once when its queue is empty, then only the pages that hold the picture.
steps.done_when: A unit test of the save action with next/cache stubbed sees a body-only publish call updateTag with page:{id} and not pages:{store}, a unit test of the alt-text route sees at most one store-wide refresh across 10 runs (10 today), and the ratchet's count of places that refresh the store-wide tag is under 55.

Do it after step 2.14, so the week is set on the final tags, and let use-cache.scan.test.ts hold each read's life.

steps.title: Keep a page's title and flags in columns

Add stored generated columns on commerce.pages in one migration (add only), and read them in publishedPageNames() and usesRememberedModals().

steps.what: The admin's page lists, pickers and AI tools read two whole documents a page (the draft and the published copy) at 16 call sites. A grid of pages or articles reads whole documents to draw its cards. listPages() reads list fields from the columns of step 2.16 and pages at 100. A grid selects its cards' facts in SQL and fetches a document only for a row with neither an excerpt nor a description.
steps.done_when: 'select id, slug, draft, published' is in src/server/pages.ts only inside getPageForEdit(), and an integration test draws a 24-article grid whose articles have excerpts and reads no published document.

steps.title: Read a cold store page's frame in one wave
steps.what: A cold frame asks about 20 statements, some one after another and one per optional feature whether the store uses it or not; siteCookies() alone asks 8 or 9 in a row. Start the independent reads together. Fold the feature questions into one site-facts read (src/server/site-facts.ts) that keeps the tags of the readers it replaces. Take menu titles from the page index of step 0.24 and the modal flag from the column of step 2.16, and let a search read its rules once.

steps.title: Read nothing that grows with the catalogue, and read the cart and checkout in one wave
steps.what: No finding covers the catalogue's reads or a cart with lines and the checkout, so the plan brings code review steps 3.8 to 3.10 in with numbers. The front page's JSON-LD comes from a small cached read of handles, never the product summaries. Product metadata takes its market codes from getProduct(). tolerated.why: Eleven hand-written claim-with-a-lease statements, about 130 lines in all. Each has another table, join and retry column: an idiom, not a copy. Tolerance: the 11 are held as a count by the copy baseline of step 1.17 and may not rise.

The Stripe and Supabase SDKs load with 97% of routes: 18 to 28 ms and about 1 MB of heap on a lean route, nothing a person sees. Step 2.22 takes Stripe off the read of a store, the graph test of step 1.8 shows the edges that are left, and they are cut when stores.ts or stripe.ts is next changed.

All of react-dom (8.1 MB) rides in four PDF traces of 107 to 140 MB: 5 to 7% of them and nothing a person feels, and a wrong glob would break invoices. The trace report of step 1.8 shows the number; act only if a function nears Vercel's size limit.

The default icon is 26 KB raw, about 9 KB on the wire, fetched at low priority after load, once per site, and only by a store with no icon of its own. It delays nothing a shopper sees, and it gets a day's cache lifetime with the public files in step 0.32.

40% of the built client files are second copies of modules, but a browser meets about 14% of that while moving around the admin, and it is the chunker working as designed. The only lever is an experimental flag on a build with no memory to spare. The plan's other steps remove about 1.5 MB of the 6.89 MB of copies. Measure again after them, and adopt the flag only if a 59-screen tour falls by 10% or more with no budget raised.

Every one of these reads is cached and tagged, and together they cost about 1.5 s of database time a day. The uncached part, the AI provider row, is closed by step 0.21, and the modal scan by step 2.16. Tolerance: a cached, tagged read may fetch a row wider than it shows while the row is under about 10 KB.

About 290 KB and 10 ms per cold instance, and the only cut in the set that could show a shopper the wrong language. Tolerance: all four hand-written storefront languages load with a page, 0.4 MB of its 4 MB budget. Look again when a fifth hand-written language is added.

A crawler asks for each store's robots.txt, sitemap, llms.txt and feed about once a day, so a one-hour CDN window would save almost nothing. What a cold sitemap costs is what it reads, and step 0.24 removes most of that. Add the header when the handlers are next opened.

Raw status checks kept for 91 days are bounded: about 131,000 rows and 20 MB at steady state, in the platform's own table, pruned, and not growing with stores. Its one-line fix (bound the newest-check read to one day) is made when status.ts is opened for step 3.5.

It names a pattern, not a cost of its own: 341 loops hold a database call. All but the per-site job loops run over a parent's few rows, and their cost follows use. The per-site loops are closed by steps 0.27, 0.28, 3.3 and 3.6, and the budget of step 1.10 holds the tolerance as a number: at most 2 more statements a tick for each added store with chat and pictures on.

53 of 110 store links and 133 of 254 AI tools stand behind no switch. That is fine: a switch changes what an owner sees, not what a store costs. Links hide in Basic, a round is capped whatever is switched, and jobs are set-based. Where a feature does cost an idle store the fix is at the read (step 0.22), and the surface budget of step 1.18 asks each new feature for its idle cost. No second tier of switches.

Campaigns (7 kinds) and discount codes (3 kinds) are two mechanisms with a shared edge, not one job built twice: about 100 to 200 lines of parallel helpers, in code that decides money. Fold the helpers into one small module when pricing code is next opened. The one Discounts page is already code review step 2.4.

The parity-wave workflow has not run since feature waves were paused on 29 October, so no session pays for it. Its fix is three edits (cap the spec at 30,000 characters, tell agents to read sections 1 to 5 and their own part, drop the draft of a CLAUDE.md bullet), to make on the day a wave is next run.

motion.css stays in the sheet: 18.7 KB raw, 3.8 KB Brotli on a first visit, also for a store with no builder motion. Taking it out needs a build step and a second render-blocking request on every page that does use motion, and nobody can know the share before opening. The stylesheet budget holds it. Look again when the reading of step 1.23 shows under half of published pages need it.

A deliberate, written design (D312 A6 and A8): the server answers in English because the AI manager and the tests read it, and about 300 refusals are matched back to their Norwegian. It costs 16.7 KB of source kept twice and no measurable time. The one real mismatch, the product.media pair, is settled in step 0.36. Add the coverage test when a validator is next changed.
